items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: a couple of duettists named Vared and Bailly made up the rest of the show. We played the first four dates in Belgium...

ctx.x: The stars of this show were Felix Leclerc, a French Canadian Singer and composer and André Claveau, who was a very popular music hall and radio singer. Another person who was to become a big star later was a comedian named Fernand Raynaud.

Jack Gauthier was quite well known fantasist and singer. Rose Mania was also with the show; a woman named Paulette Lancry and a couple of duettists named Vared and Bailly made up the rest of the show. We played the first four dates in Belgium, then we went to Lille, Roubaix and Bethune. Our success with the public was as great, if not greater than the stars, and we were put under a certain pressure by Rose Mania and Henri Lecca. We went on before Rose and di only three numbers, closing with the Saint Louis Blues.…

Felix Leclerc was a very quiet and nice person to be with. Jack Gauthier, gay and full of life but André Claveau was very temperamental and playing big star. The show was often back stage as much as in the hall and it was very funny.
